question: Which of the following reports or missions mainly recommended that control over some aspects of provincial government be passed to Indian ministers responsible to an Indian electorate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Montagu Chelmsford report**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** was a significant document in the history of British India, aimed at reforming the structure of the Indian government.
 
• It recommended the introduction of **dual governance**, known as **Diarchy**, in the provinces. This system divided the subjects of administration into two categories: **reserved** and **transferred**.
 
• Under the diarchy system, **Indian ministers** were given control over the transferred subjects, which included **education, health, and local self-government**.
 
• The report advocated for increased **Indian participation** in the administration of the country, with Indian ministers being responsible to an **Indian electorate**.
 
• The reforms recommended by the Montagu-Chelmsford Report were enacted through the **Government of India Act 1919**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Morley Minto report**__

 __
 
• The **Morley-Minto Reforms**, also known as the **Indian Councils Act 1909**, aimed to increase Indian representation in the government but did not propose significant transfer of power to Indian ministers.
 
• This act introduced the concept of **separate electorates** for Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Cripps' Mission**__
 __
 
• The **Cripps' Mission** was sent to India in 1942 during World War II, with proposals for Indian self-government post-war but did not specifically address the transfer of provincial government control to Indian ministers.
 
• The mission failed as its proposals were rejected by the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission report**__
 
 
• The **Simon Commission** was set up in 1927 to review the working of the Government of India Act 1919, but it did not include any Indians, leading to widespread protests.
 
• The commission's report led to the enactment of the Government of India Act 1935.
